title: Affiliate software pricing: why "unlimited" rarely means unlimited
summary: Dustin Howes interviews the CEO of TrackDesk about hidden ceilings in affiliate platform pricing. His framing: "unlimited" on a pricing page is a hook, and click caps, contact-sales walls and overages are where growing programs get burned. Most substance comes from the guest; Dustin's contribution is the buyer's checklist.

principles.text: Treat "unlimited" on an affiliate software pricing page as a claim to verify, not a fact.
principles.quote: I've been burned by this before in some of my affiliate programs where unlimited on the pricing page doesn't really mean unlimited.

principles.text: Ask vendors on the record where their unlimited promise has a ceiling, such as click caps or contact-sales walls.
principles.quote: Every vendor in this category says unlimited somewhere in their pricing page. Fewer of them will tell you on the record where that promise actually has a ceiling.

principles.text: Pricing surprises hit hardest once the program starts working, so evaluate what happens to the bill at scale before signing.
principles.quote: That gap is exactly where a lot of growing programs get burned.

principles.text: Click-based overage pricing is risky because forced or fraudulent clicks inflate usage, and not every vendor will reverse them.
principles.quote: There could be force clicks. There could be some kind of nefarious actions going on and not every network is will listen when you try to bring that up and try to get those reversed.
